documents.title: Transitional care call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Post-discharge call (rehab discharge 1/23). Spoke with patient; sister on speaker. Home since Friday, sister staying through the week. Walking in the apartment with her cane, no falls. Speech a little slurred but she is understood fine on the phone. Home infusion nurse came Saturday, TPN running nightly without problems. Home PT/OT starts this week.
Meds reviewed against rehab summary: bupropion XL 150 daily, lamotrigine 100 bid, alprazolam 0.25 prn, diphenhydramine 25 qhs prn, MVI, TPN. GI infusion center has her vedolizumab booked 2/10. Sertraline stopped in hospital — she knows not to restart it.
No confusion, headache, vomiting. Appt with PCP Wed 1/28 confirmed.

events.reason: Transitional care after hospitalization and rehab

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit — hospital 11/7–12/5/2025, inpatient rehab 12/5/2025–1/23/2026. Discharge summaries reviewed in full.

Summary: found confused at home, Na 112 → SIADH (sertraline stopped). Na rose to 129 over 48 h on IV saline; on hospital day 3 became unresponsive — MRI 11/12 central pontine myelinolysis. ICU, no intubation, slow recovery of eye, limb and speech function. Rehab 7 weeks, now home walking with a cane.

Today: here with sister. Gets around the apartment with the cane, uses it everywhere for now. Speech slower and a bit slurred. Doing her own TPN connections with the infusion nurse checking. Home PT/OT started. Mood "honestly, scared, but glad to be home." No seizures. No thoughts of self-harm.

Meds reconciled: bupropion XL 150 daily; lamotrigine 100 bid (continued through the hospital stay); alprazolam 0.25 prn; diphenhydramine 25 qhs prn; MVI; TPN nightly; vedolizumab q8wk, next infusion 2/10 (deferred during the admission). Sertraline discontinued.
Allergies: NSAIDs (GI intolerance, ineffective); gabapentin (ineffective).

Exam: vitals reviewed. Weight 53.0 (58.7 in July). Alert, oriented, follows all commands. Speech mildly dysarthric, fully intelligible. Extraocular movements full. Moves all extremities, strength grossly full. Gait mildly unsteady, steady with cane. Line site clean. Lungs clear.
PHQ-9 11.

A/P:
1. Central pontine myelinolysis — recovering. Home PT/OT. Neurology follow-up referral placed. Fall precautions.
2. Hyponatremia/SIADH — resolved. BMP today. Sertraline off; no other SSRI without discussing with psych and us.
3. MDD, recurrent, partial remission — on bupropion alone now. Psych appointment in March; message sent to her psychiatrist about the sertraline stop.
4. Weight down almost 6 kg — GI and home infusion aware; recheck at each visit.
5. Former smoker since 8/2025 — still not smoking.
RTC 6 weeks.

documents.title: Sodium result

documents.body: Hi Tracy — your sodium and the rest of the electrolytes and kidney function from Wednesday are normal. Keep doing what you're doing with the home therapists.

Reviewed — goals: safe household and community ambulation with cane, independent home exercise program, fall prevention. Signed and returned by fax.

documents.title: Parking placard
documents.author: patient
documents.body:
My sister says I can get a handicap parking placard for when she drives me. Can you fill out the form? I'll drop it off.
— Tracy

Reply (front desk): Yes — drop it at the front desk and the doctor will complete it within a few days.
Follow-up note (front desk 2/23): State disability placard application completed by PCP (temporary, 1 year), patient picked up.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Six weeks home. Home PT wrapping up; she walks the hallway of her building without the cane now, uses it outside. No falls. Speech "people still notice." Mood up and down; misses being independent. Psych visit 3/23. Sleeping ok with diphenhydramine. Not smoking.
O: Vitals reviewed. Weight about the same as January. Mild dysarthria. Gait mildly unsteady without cane, steady with it. Line site clean.
A/P:
- CPM — improving. Neurology April. Home exercise program after PT ends.
- Na normal in January; BMP today.
- MDD — bupropion; psych later this month.
- Weight — holding steady; GI following. Vedolizumab resumed 2/10.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient Psychiatry — 03/23/2026

First visit since her hospitalization for hyponatremia complicated by central pontine myelinolysis; sertraline was stopped by the inpatient team because of SIADH. She has stayed on bupropion XL 150 mg. Mood is lower than last summer but she is not in a major relapse: some sadness and worry about her recovery, sleep and appetite fair, no psychotic symptoms, no thoughts of death.

Assessment: major depressive disorder, recurrent, in partial remission; GAD.

Plan: continue bupropion XL 150 mg alone for now; we will not restart an SSRI given the SIADH. Alprazolam sparingly. Weekly supportive therapy with our clinic social worker. Return in 2 months.

Outpatient Psychiatry

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROLOGY — RETURN VISIT
Date of service: 04/13/2026

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Bianchi is seen five months after central pontine myelinolysis, which followed correction of severe hyponatremia in November. We follow her yearly for temporal lobe epilepsy on lamotrigine 100 mg twice daily, which was continued throughout her hospitalization; she reports no seizures since 2020.

She has continued to improve since leaving rehabilitation in January. She walks indoors without an aid and uses a cane outdoors only. Speech is clearer, with mild residual slurring. No swallowing difficulty.

Examination: alert and fully oriented. Mild dysarthria. Extraocular movements full. Strength and sensation normal in all limbs. Gait mildly unsteady, able to walk without the cane in clinic.

Impression: central pontine myelinolysis with continued recovery; residual mild dysarthria and mild gait unsteadiness. Temporal lobe epilepsy without events on lamotrigine.

Plan: continue lamotrigine 100 mg twice daily. Continue home exercises; outpatient therapy if progress stalls. Follow up in 6 months.

Sincerely,
Neurology

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video check-in. Neurology 4/13: continued recovery, cane outdoors only, f/u 6 mo. Psych 3/23: bupropion alone, weekly therapy — she's going and "it helps to talk." Walking to the corner store with her cane. Speech sounds clearer to me than in March. Eating well, TPN nightly. No seizures.
Plan: physical in July. GI visit next month.

documents.title: Intestinal Rehabilitation Clinic Letter
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Intestinal Rehabilitation — follow-up 06/08/2026

Dear Doctor,

Seen earlier than her usual annual visit after her prolonged hospitalization last winter. TPN was continued throughout and she is back on her usual nightly 12-hour infusion through the same tunneled catheter, which has had no infections or occlusions. Crohn's remains quiet on vedolizumab; the infusion due during her hospital stay was given 02/10 after she came home, and she is back on her every-8-week schedule. Weight has been recovering since discharge. Home infusion labs acceptable. No formula change.

Colonoscopy is due in 2027.

Return in one year.

Gastroenterology / Intestinal Rehabilitation

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PREVENTIVE VISIT — 51F

The year: SIADH with Na 112 in 11/2025, central pontine myelinolysis after correction, ICU then 7 weeks inpatient rehab, home 1/23. Sertraline stopped. Since then steady recovery — neurology 4/13 pleased. Psych on bupropion alone plus weekly therapy. GI 6/8, TPN unchanged. Not smoking since 8/2025. Drinks a cocktail on some weekends.

Meds: bupropion XL 150 daily; lamotrigine 100 bid; alprazolam 0.25 prn (a few times a month); diphenhydramine 25 qhs prn; multivitamin; TPN nightly; vedolizumab q8wk (GI).
Allergies: NSAIDs (GI intolerance, ineffective); gabapentin (ineffective).
Problems: Crohn's on vedolizumab/short bowel/TPN with tunneled line; recurrent MDD in partial remission; GAD; temporal lobe epilepsy on lamotrigine (no events since 2020); hx CPM with mild residual dysarthria and gait unsteadiness; R superior gluteal nerve palsy; chronic LBP; hx provoked PE 2023; s/p cholecystectomy 2022.

ROS: no headaches, no falls, no swallowing trouble, no chest pain or dyspnea, no leg swelling.

Exam: Weight 55.5 (53.0 in January). Mild dysarthria. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed scars. Tunneled line site clean. No edema. Walks without the cane in the office, mildly unsteady, mild R hip drop. Mood euthymic today, affect reactive.
PHQ-9 9, GAD-7 9, AUDIT-C 2.

Plan:
- Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c, Mg, B12, D, iron.
- Mammogram — last 3/2025; ordered now.
- Pap/HPV due 2027; colonoscopy due 2027 with GI.
- Flu and COVID vaccines this fall.
- Fall prevention reviewed; keep home exercise program.
- Continue psych/neuro/GI plans.
RTC September.
